Check that suppressed cells cannot be recovered

check_suppression.Rd

Suppressing a small cell only helps if it cannot be worked out from the rest of the table. When a row or column has a total and only one suppressed cell, the cell is the total minus the others. This check follows every line of the table that has a total (a row or column labelled "Total", "All", "I alt", ...), recovers what can be recovered, and repeats, because a recovered cell can open the next line. The usual fix is secondary suppression: suppress a second cell in each line, or remove the totals.

Usage

check_suppression(x, by = NULL, count = NULL, config = NULL, target = NULL)

Arguments

x

An aggregated table: a data frame with a count column, or a table.

by

Grouping variables. For an aggregated table the default is all non-numeric columns.

count

Name of the count column in an aggregated table. Detected automatically when a column is called n, count, freq or similar. Leave NULL with by for microdata.

config

A mimic_config(); NULL uses the defaults.

target

Label used in reports.

Value

A mimic_check. details lists the cells that can be recovered, by label.

Details

Suppressed cells are NA or written as "<5", ".", "..", "x" or "*". Totals released in another table are not seen here; see check_differencing() and the register in inspect().

See also

Other checks: check_differencing(), check_dominance(), check_extremes(), check_group_disclosure(), check_k_anonymity(), check_keys(), check_min_count(), check_model()

Examples

tab <- data.frame(sex = c("F", "M", "Total"), n = c(NA, 120, 123))
check_suppression(tab)
#> ✖ suppression (tab): 1 of 1 suppressed cell(s) can be recovered from the totals; suppress a second cell in each line or remove the totals.
#>  sex
#>    F

# a second suppressed cell protects the first
tab$n[2] <- NA
check_suppression(tab)
#> ✔ suppression (tab): 2 suppressed cell(s) cannot be recovered from the totals in the table.
